title: RWB-TE-007 content is outdated under D-RCV-60
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Technical Enablers v2.md
description: v2 describes Quartz, a clustered Quartz job store and shared job tables. Template and Rules section R6 retires RWB-TE-007 with no new story, and Arch v5 slide 44 replaces Quartz with a Temporal Schedule or an event-started workflow in the owning service.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 section R6 (Retired: RWB-TE-007, dependencies point to RWB-PLT-E1071-CON); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44
proposed: Keep the section with a retirement banner and a step-by-step target table; the work moves to RWB-PLT-E1071-CON.

title: The 79 specified operations are not divided between the 19 API files
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Technical Enablers v2.md
section: RWB-TE-003 Types and contract tests from the API specification
description: v2 counts 79 operations in one api/recovery-api.yaml. Template and Rules section R8.4 splits the specification into 19 service files plus gateway-bff and an index, and no source states how many of the 79 operations each service owns.
evidence: RWB-TE-003 step 8 (79 specified operations); Template and Rules v1 section R8.4 (API Specification split into 19 files plus gateway-bff and an index)
proposed: Keep 79 as the total across the files and take each service count from its own API file once the split is approved.

title: The performance mix does not name the owning service of its 7 operations
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Technical Enablers v2.md
description: The mix of 7 operations and the 410 users were sized against one endpoint base. In the target each operation is called one hop through gateway-bff to its owner service, and no source states which of the 19 services owns each of the 7 operations or how the 2 s budget is shared.
evidence: RWB-TE-009 steps 5 to 8; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 20 (one hop, 2 s timeout per service)
proposed: Keep the 7 operations, the weights and the limits; map each operation to its owner service from the OperationCatalog of RWB-PLT-TE003-APP before the first gated run.

title: One code owners file or one per repository is not stated
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Technical Enablers v2.md
section: RWB-TE-002 Code owners for the recovery module
description: v2 places one .github/CODEOWNERS at the repository root. The target has 19 service repositories plus ace-web and the architecture repository, and no source states whether each repository carries its own file or one shared file is used. The team handles themselves stay assumed until DL37 and DL36 are answered.
evidence: RWB-TE-002 step 1; Template and Rules v1 section R6 and the 19 service repositories of Arch v5 slide 41
proposed: One code owners file per repository with the same team handles, applied by RWB-PLT-TE002-OPS.

title: The owner of the outbox admin endpoints after the split is not stated
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Technical Enablers v2.md
section: RWB-TE-006 Outbox and retry for outbound work
description: The GET and POST admin endpoints read deliveries across the estate, while the outbox and inbox tables become library objects in every service schema (Ownership Map: owner PLT). No source states which service serves those endpoints in the target, or how a cross-service delivery list is composed.
evidence: RWB-TE-006 step 9; Ownership Map Tables outbox_delivery and outbox_event (owner PLT, one copy per service schema)
proposed: Serve the endpoints from rwb-integration against the library, or from the platform library host if the ownership ruling places them there; decide before the first EXCEPTION delivery is handled.
